Bogdanović''' ({{lang-sr-cyr|Богдан Богдановић}}; born 18 August 1992) is a Serbian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He also represents the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national team]]. He was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 27th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]], with his draft rights being traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] during the [[2016 NBA draft]]. Bogdanović earned an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]], a [[FIBA EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-FIBA EuroBasket Team]] and was selected two times to the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-FIBA World Cup First Team]]. He helped Serbia win the bronze medal and was named to the [[FIBA Men's Olympics All-Star Five#FIBA All-Second Team by tournament|FIBA Olympics All-Second Team]] at [[2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics in Paris]]. He is the all-time leading scorer for Serbia. ==Early life, family and education == {{expand-section | date = March 2026}} Bogdan Bogdanović was born in Serbia. He is related to the Serbian [[architect]] [[Bogdan Bogdanović (architect)|Bogdan Bogdanović]], sharing the same name. ==Early career== Bogdanović began playing organized basketball with ŠKK Zvezdara, a club in [[Belgrade]]. In April 2008, he moved on to [[KK Žitko Basket|Žitko Basket]] (then known as Alimenti Basket), also from Belgrade. Playing with Žitko Basket under coach [[Dragan Jakovljević (basketball)|Dragan Jakovljević]], Bogdanović was part of the team that in April 2010 earned third place in the 2009–10 Junior Serbian League at the final eight tournament in [[Vršac]],{{cite news | url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2010&mm=04&dd=18&nav_id=425287 | title=Novi Sad juniorski prvak Srbije | publisher=[[B92]]| date=18 April 2010 | access-date=2 May 2015|language=sr}}{{cite news | url=http://www.vesti-online.com/Sport/Kosarka/375925/Bogdanovic-nudjen-Zvezdi-odbili-ga-kao-netalentovanog | title=Bogdanović nuđen Zvezdi, odbili ga kao netalentovanog! | publisher=Frankfurtske Vesti| date=20 January 2014 | access-date=2 May 2015|language=sr}} after beating [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] juniors in the quarterfinal, losing 89–86 to [[KK Hemofarm|Hemofarm]] juniors in the semifinal and beating [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|FMP]] junior team 82–76 in the third place game. A few weeks later in May 2010, together with another Žitko player Luka Pajković, Bogdanović got attached to FMP's junior team featuring [[Nenad Miljenović]], [[Stefan Popovski-Turanjanin]], [[Nemanja Bezbradica]], [[Nikola Janković (basketball)|Nikola Janković]], and Nikola Silađi for the [[Euroleague Basketball Nike International Junior Tournament|Nike International Junior Tournament]] (NIJT) in [[Paris]] where the FMP juniors were defending their club's double title from the previous two years. They were drawn in one of two round-robin groups at the tournament, alongside [[KK Split]], [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Treviso]], and [[Baloncesto Málaga|Málaga]]. After beating Treviso and Split, FMP required a win over [[Baloncesto Málaga|Málaga]] juniors to win their group and make the final; with precisely Bogdanović making the difference with an off-balance buzzer-beater for a 79–78 final score, two of his 21 points on the day alongside 6 rebounds.{{cite web|title=Nike Invitational Junior Tournament pits defending champs FMP against hometown INSEP |url=http://www.ballineurope.com/european-basketball/euroleague/nike-invitational-junior-tournament-pits-defending-champs-fmp-belgrad-vs-insep-6297/ |work=ballineurope.com |access-date=24 April 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140425030019/http://www.ballineurope.com/european-basketball/euroleague/nike-invitational-junior-tournament-pits-defending-champs-fmp-belgrad-vs-insep-6297/ |archive-date=25 April 2014 }}[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=84&seasoncode=JT09#!boxscore Malaga – FMP 88:79];NIJT, May 2010 In the final game FMP took on [[INSEP]] and lost 73–83[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=87&seasoncode=JT09#!boxscore INSEP – FMP 83:73];NIJT, 9 May 2010 with Bogdanović having an outing to forget due to the mid-game injury that forced him to leave the contest. ==Professional career== ===Partizan (2010–2014)=== In September 2010, 18-year-old Bogdanović signed his first professional contract with [[KK Partizan|Partizan]].{{cite news | url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2010&mm=09&dd=17&nav_id=459524 | title=Bogdan Bogdanović u Partizanu | publisher=b92.net| date=17 September 2010 | access-date=6 October 2013|language=sr}} Initially, in his first two seasons with the ''crno-beli'', under head coach [[Vlada Jovanović]], Bogdanović didn't play much. With the summer 2012 return of head coach [[Duško Vujošević]] to Partizan, 20-year-old Bogdanović began to see increased minutes. After [[Danilo Anđušić]]'s departure in December 2012, Bogdanović's role in the team stabilized even more. The 2012–13 season saw him make his [[2012–13 Euroleague|EuroLeague]] debut with the team, averaging 5 points per game and 1.8 rebounds per game over 6 appearances. After being called up for the Serbian national team during summer 2013, he earned greater trust from coach Vujošević, reflected in increased playing time and bigger team role in the 2013–14 season. In the EuroLeague victory over [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in Belgrade, Bogdanović scored a career-high 27 points, shooting 10 for 16 from the field.{{cite web|title=Partizan NIS Belgrade vs. CSKA 30.8 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 4.2 assists per game. For such a performance, he was named the league's Finals MVP.{{cite web|title=Bogdan: "Titula za devojčicu sa VMA!"|url=http://www.sportske.net/vest/kosarka/bogdan-titula-za-devojcicu-sa-vma-183979.html|website=sportske.net|access-date=21 June 2014|language=sr}} Following Bogdanović's summer 2014 transfer from Partizan to Fenerbahce, the player's decision to leave the club was publicly criticized by Partizan's head coach Vujošević who claimed that by leaving in 2014 Bogdanović broke their verbal agreement the coach had struck with the player (along with Bogdanović's parents and agent Aleksandar Rašković) two years earlier in 2012.{{cite news|title=Partizan opet sarađuje sa agentom Raškovićem|url=http://mondo.rs/a830402/Sport/Kosarka/Adin-Vrabac-trenira-sa-Partizanom.html|access-date=16 September 2015|work=mondo.rs|date=15 September 2015}} Their 2012 agreement, according to the coach, saw then 20-year-old Bogdanović be placed immediately into Partizan's first team rotation in return for the player's promise he would stay with the team three more seasons from that point on. Following Partizan's failure to qualify for the [[2014–15 Euroleague|next season's EuroLeague]], Bogdanović left the club in summer 2014—two years after the supposed agreement thus one year short of the 3-year commitment. ===Fenerbahçe (2014–2017)=== On 11 July 2014, Bogdanović officially signed a four-year contract, containing opt-out clauses after the second and third seasons, with the Turkish team [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]].{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce lands Rising Star Bogdanovic|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138318/180|access-date=11 July 2014|work=Euroleague.net}}{{cite news|title=Bogdan Bogdanovic Fenerbahçe Ülker'de|url=http://www.fenerbahce.org/fbulker/detay.asp?ContentID=40746|language=tr|access-date=11 July 2014|work=fenerbahce.org}} Over four years, Bogdanović is slated to make [[€]]3.5 million euros net income, while Partizan also received a €1.3 million buyout from Fenerbahçe, as the player was still under contract with the Belgrade club.{{cite web|title=Bogdanović otišao na potpisivanje ugovora sa Fenerom!|url=http://www.sportske.net/vest/kosarka/bogdanovic-otisao-na-potpisivanje-ugovora-sa-fenerom-186531.html|website=sportske.net|access-date=11 July 2014|language=sr}} ====2014–15 season==== Even though Bogdanović was a newcomer in the team, head coach [[Željko Obradović]] gave him a significant number of minutes and a starter role. With the beginning of the 2014–15 season, he struggled in shooting and consistency.{{cite news|last=Avdić|first=Edin|url=http://mondo.rs/a780748/Kolumne/Edin-Avdic/Edin-Avdic-kolumna-Zeljko-Obradovic-i-Fenerbahce.html|title=Njih 30 miliona i Željko|agency=mondo.rs|date=24 March 2015|access-date=25 March 2015}} On 15 November, in a 93–86 win over [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|FC Bayern Munich]], he scored 18 points and added 7 assists, his best game since coming to the new team.{{cite news|title=Goudelock sets record as Fenerbahce wins in Munich|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=56&pcode=002821&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=22 November 2014|work=euroleague.net}} Over 10 games in the [[2014–15 Euroleague Regular Season Group C|first phase]] of the EuroLeague, he averaged 10.4 points and 3.4 assists per game. On 20 March, Bogdanović set a season-high of 25 points, and added 4 assists, in a 98–77 win over [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Emporio Armani Milano]].{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce Ulker claims playoff spot with ninth straight win|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=208&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=20 March 2015|work=euroleague.net}} For such a performance, he was named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round]], with a [[Performance Index Rating]] of 32.{{cite news|title=Top 16 Round 11 bwin MVP: Bogdan Bogdanovic, Fenerbahce Ulker Istanbul|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5txpoh5xh3595swk/top-16-round-11-bwin-mvp-bogdan-bogdanovic-fenerbahce-ulker-istanbul|access-date=21 March 2015|work=euroleague.net}} On 26 March, in a game against [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]], he scored a 20-meter distance [[buzzer beater]] at the end of the second quarter.{{cite news|title=Bogdanov koš sa celog terena!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=03&dd=26&nav_id=973376|access-date=26 March 2015|work=b92.net|language=sr}} After good showings in the [[2014–15 Euroleague Top 16 Group F|Top 16]], he struggled in shooting in the [[2014–15 Euroleague Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] playoff series against [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], averaging 8 points on 25% shooting from the field. Eventually, Fenerbahçe won the EuroLeague playoff series, and advanced to the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four]], the first in the club's history.{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce for the first time in the Final Four|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/2015/04/league-action/87436/|access-date=15 May 2015|work=eurohoops.net|date=20 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518101508/http://www.eurohoops.net/2015/04/league-action/87436/|archive-date=18 May 2015}} On 7 May, he was voted the [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] for the second season in a row, becoming only the second player, after [[Nikola Mirotić]], to win the award twice.{{cite news|title=Euroleague Rising Star Trophy: Bogdan Bogdanovic, Fenerbahce Ulker Istanbul|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xr5u88astihvwuj|access-date=7 May 2015|work=euroleague.net}} On 15 May 2015, however, his team lost in the EuroLeague semifinal game to [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], by a score of 87–96.{{cite news|title=Real Madrid heads to third straight final after beating Fenerbahce|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=248&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=15 May 2015|work=euro–league.net|date=15 May 2015}} Eventually, Fenerbahçe finished in 4th place in the EuroLeague, after losing in the third-place game to [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], by a score of 80–86.{{cite news|title=CSKA Moscow beats Fenerbahce in third-place game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report|access-date=18 May 2015|work=euroleague.net|date=17 May 2015}} Over the season, in 29 EuroLeague games, Bogdanović averaged 10.6 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game. Also, in 36 games of the [[2014–15 Turkish Basketball League|Turkish League]], he averaged 11.5 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 2.4 assists. ====2015–16 season==== Throughout his second season with the team, Bogdanović continued with his good performances, becoming one of the team's leaders. Occasionally, in the late phases of the games, he also had the ball in his hands. Fenerbahçe won the [[Turkish Cup Basketball|Turkish Cup]], with a 67–65 win over [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]], with Bogdanović being named the [[Turkish Basketball Cup MVP|Cup MVP]]. Fenerbahçe also reached [[EuroLeague Finals|the final game]] of the [[2016 Euroleague Final Four]], but fell short of winning the EuroLeague championship, after an [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] 96–101 loss to [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].{{cite web|title=CSKA Moscow claims its seventh Euroleague crown after OT thriller|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2015#!report |website=Euroleague.net |date=15 May 2016 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20160516061653/http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2015%23!report |archivedate=16 May 2016 |url-status=dead |access-date=9 September 2016}} Over 28 EuroLeague games, he averaged 11.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 3 assists per game. At the end of the season, Fenerbahçe won the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish League]] championship. ====2016–17 season==== On 26 October 2016, in a [[2016–17 EuroLeague|EuroLeague]] game against [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]], Bogdanović sprained his right ankle; at first it was estimated that he will need two to three weeks of recovery time,{{cite news|title=Bogdanović nije ozbiljnije povređen|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2016&mm=10&dd=27&nav_id=1192816|access-date=27 October 2016|work=b92.net|date=27 October 2016|language=sr}} but recovery didn't seem to go as expected as he didn't return until January 2017.{{cite news|title=Bogdan Bogdanović, as Fenerbahčea, za "Blic": Bez mene protiv Zvezde|url=http://sport.blic.rs/evroliga-1617/bogdan-bogdanovic-as-fenerbahcea-za-blic-bez-mene-protiv-zvezde/9t065yt|access-date=14 December 2016|work=Blic|date=7 December 2016|language=sr}} On 6 January 2017, he returned on the court, in a game against [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Milano]]. Bogdanović proved to be a major contributor for Fenerbahçe in the EuroLeague playoffs, as he would be the team's leading scorer in their first two games against [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], before his club ultimately swept them, to earn another [[EuroLeague Final Four]] appearance. As a result of his contributions, he was not only named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round|EuroLeague's Player of the Round]] during those first two playoff games, but he was also named the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month|EuroLeague's Player of the Month]], for his overall work that month.{{cite news|title=Turkish Airlines EuroLeague MVP for April: Bogdan Bogdanovic, Fenerbahce Istanbul|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7sdgsfth7fjly3r9/turkish-airlines-euroleague-mvp-for-april-bogdan-bogdanovic-fenerbahce-istanbul|access-date=27 May 2017|work=Euroleague.net|date=4 May 2017}} He later helped Fenerbahçe repeat their place in the [[EuroLeague Finals|Finals of the EuroLeague]], after helping them defeat [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], in the EuroLeague Final Four semifinals, by a score of 84–75. He had 14 points and 6 rebounds against Real Madrid. Two days later, Bogdanović would help the club win their first ever [[EuroLeague]] championship, as they beat out [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], by a score of 80–64, in [[2017 EuroLeague Final Four|the championship game]]. Afterwards, Bogdanović would lead Fenerbahçe to its second straight Turkish Super League Finals victory, by sweeping [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Sompo Japan]], and winning the [[Turkish Basketball Super League Finals MVP|Turkish Super League Finals MVP]] award in the process. In 2020, he was named to the [[EuroLeague 2010–20 All-Decade Team]].{{Cite web|title=Bogdan Bogdanovic named on the EuroLeague All-Decade Team|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1056421/bogdan-bogdanovic-named-on-the-euroleague-all-decade-team/|date=5 May 2020|website=Eurohoops|language=en|access-date=5 May 2020}}{{Cite web|title=Богдан уврштен у Евролигин тим деценије|url=http://www.rts.rs/page/sport/ci/story/32/kosarka/3943789/bogdan-bogdanovic-evroliga-tim-decenije.html|author=((RTS, Radio televizija Srbije, Radio Television of Serbia))|website=rts.rs|access-date=5 May 2020}} ===Sacramento Kings (2017–2020)=== On 26 June 2014, while playing for Partizan Belgrade, Bogdanović was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 27th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-pick-bogdan-bogdanovic-27th-selection|title=Suns Pick Up Bogdan Bogdanovic With 27th Selection|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=26 June 2014|access-date=27 June 2014}} On 23 June 2016, on the night of the [[2016 NBA draft]], the Suns traded his rights to the [[Sacramento Kings]] along with [[Georgios Papagiannis]], [[Skal Labissière]] and the [[Detroit Pistons]]' 2020 second-round pick, in exchange for the draft rights of [[Marquese Chriss]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-draft-night-trade|title=Kings Announce Draft-Night Trade|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=23 June 2016|access-date=3 July 2016}} On 13 July 2017, Bogdanović signed a three-year, $27 million contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite news|title=Kings Sign Bogdan Bogdanovic|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-bogdan-bogdanovic|access-date=13 July 2017|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=13 July 2017}} He made his NBA debut on 23 October 2017, against the team that originally drafted him, the [[Phoenix Suns]]. Bogdanović recorded 12 points, 3 rebounds, and 2 assists in 25 minutes of play off the bench as the Kings lost 117–115.{{cite news|title=Bookers Suns top Kings 117–115 for 1st win|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974799|access-date=24 October 2017|publisher=ESPN|date=24 October 2017}} Bogdanović was selected as a member of the Team World for the [[2018 NBA All-Star Game|2018]] [[Rising Stars Challenge]]. He led Team World to a 155–124 win over Team USA with 26 points, 6 assists and 4 rebounds, while shooting 7 of 13 from the three-point line and was named the MVP of the game.{{cite news|last1=Forgave|first1=Reid|title=How Bogdan Bogdanovic shot his way to the top of Rising Stars Challenge|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/how-bogdan-bogdanovic-shot-his-way-to-the-top-of-rising-stars-challenge/|access-date=17 February 2018|work=cbssports.com|date=16 February 2018}} The Sacramento Kings finished the season with a 27–55 record, thus failing to qualify to the [[NBA playoffs]] for the twelfth season in a row. Bogdanović in his first NBA season had the averages of 11.8 points, 3.3 assists and 2.9 rebounds over 78 games. After the end of the season, he had an [[Magnetic resonance imaging|MRI]] procedure that revealed a slight tear of the [[medial meniscus]] in his left knee.{{cite news|title=Bogdan Bogdanovic Injury Update|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/bogi-update|access-date=24 April 2018|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=24 April 2018}} On 24 April 2018, he underwent a [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] [[debridement]] surgery in order to fully recover his left knee. On 22 May 2018, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].{{cite news|title=Donovan Mitchell, Ben Simmons lead 2017–18 NBA All-Rookie first team|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/05/22/all-rookie-teams-release-2017-18-season|access-date=22 May 2018|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=22 May 2018}} Bogdanović was selected as a member of the Team World for the [[2019 NBA All-Star Game|2019]] [[Rising Stars Challenge]].{{cite web |title=BOGDANOVIĆ PONOVO NA OL-STARU: Zajedno sa Dončićem u Timu sveta |url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:774418-BOGDANOVIC-PONOVO-NA-OL-STARU-Zajedno-sa-Doncicem-u-Timu-sveta |website=Večernje novosti |access-date=30 January 2019|language=sr}}{{cite web |title=Doncic, Simmons headline Mtn Dew Ice Rising Stars rosters |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/01/29/2019-mtn-dew-ice-rising-stars-roster-official-release |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=30 January 2019}} After missing the first ten games due to an injury rehab, in his sophomore season with the club Bogdanović mainly played the role of sixth man and second unit leader.{{cite news |last1=Ham |first1=James |title=Kings season in review: Breaking down Bogdan Bogdanovic's up and down year |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/kings-season-review-breaking-down-bogdan-bogdanovics-and-down-year |access-date=13 October 2019 |work=nbcsports.com |date=1 May 2019}} Over 70 games, he averaged career-highs of 14.1 points, 3.8 assists and 3.5 rebounds. In his [[Contract year phenomenon|contract year]] with the club, Bogdanović averaged 15.1 points, 3.4 assists and 3.4 rebounds over 61 games. The [[2019–20 NBA season]] was [[Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season|suspended]] in March as a result of [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and Sacramento Kings were invited for 22-team [[2020 NBA Bubble]]. Eventually, they did not manage to qualify for the [[2020 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] and finished the season with 31–41 record. ===Atlanta Hawks (2020–2025)=== In November 2020, the Kings attempted to sign-and-trade Bogdanović to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] along with [[Justin James (basketball)|Justin James]] for [[Donte DiVincenzo]], [[D. J. Wilson]], and [[Ersan İlyasova]].{{Cite web|date=20 April 2021|title=AP Source: Bucks getting Holiday to play with Antetokounmpo|url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-milwaukee-bucks-bogdan-bogdanovic-justin-james-new-orleans-pelicans-e00fe87e14afa6db14811a1a2c4d03da|access-date=23 July 2021|website=AP NEWS|language=en}}{{Cite web|date=17 November 2020|title=Sources: Bucks to acquire Holiday, Bogdanovic|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30333660/sources-milwaukee-bucks-agree-deals-new-orleans-pelicans-jrue-holiday-sacramento-kings-bogdan-bogdanovic|access-date=23 July 2021|publisher=ESPN|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Merchant|first=Sabreena|date=17 November 2020|title=Trade Grades: Bogdan Bogdanovic goes to the Bucks|url=https://www.sactownroyalty.com/2020/11/17/21571951/sacramento-kings-milwaukee-bucks-trade-grades-bogdan-bogdanovic-donte-divincenzo|access-date=23 July 2021|website=Sactown Royalty|language=en}} The trade unraveled when it was announced that the NBA was investigating the Bucks for having contact with Bogdanović and/or his agent before it was allowed under free agency rules. The Bucks reportedly felt double-crossed by the situation, decided not to pursue the trade further, and were stripped of their 2022 second-round draft pick at the conclusion of the investigation in December.{{Cite web|date=21 December 2020|title=Bucks lose 2022 2nd-round pick over early Bogdanovic talks|url=https://apnews.com/article/nba-milwaukee-bucks-basketball-justin-james-ersan-ilyasova-d5b26078818eaf60944ea31cb78c5d1f|access-date=23 July 2021|website=AP NEWS|language=en}}{{Cite magazine|last=West|first=Jenna|title=Bucks Lose 2022 Draft Pick Over Failed Bogdanovic Trade|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2020/12/21/bucks-lose-2022-draft-pick-bogdan-bogdanovic-trade-violate-tampering-rules|access-date=23 July 2021|magazine=Sports Illustrated|language=en-us}} According to Bogdanović, he was not made aware of the trade by the Kings and felt betrayed by the organization.{{Cite news|last=Amick |first=Sam |title='They screwed up': Bogdan Bogdanovic on a blown-up trade, betrayal, Kings-Bucks mess and Giannis reality |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2302892/2021/01/05/bogdan-bogdanovic-bucks-hawks-kings-trade-details/ |access-date=23 July 2021 |website=[[The Athletic]] |date=5 January 2021 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210807184817/https://theathletic.com/2302892/2021/01/05/bogdan-bogdanovic-bucks-hawks-kings-trade-details/ |archive-date=7 August 2021 |url-status=live}} On 24 November 2020, Bogdanović signed a four-year, $72 million contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-restricted-free-agent-bogdan-bogdanovic|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Restricted Free Agent Bogdan Bogdanovic|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=24 November 2020}} Bogdanović would only play in 44 games during the 2020–21 regular season due to injuries, but set new career highs, averaging 16.4 points per game and shot 90.9% on free throws. Coincidentally, the Hawks faced the Bucks in the 2021 [[NBA Conference Finals|Eastern Conference Finals]], which the Bucks won in six games before winning the [[2021 NBA Finals|NBA championship]]. After the 2021–22 season ended, Bogdanović underwent right knee surgery and was ruled out for at least three months.{{Cite magazine |title=Bogdan Bogdanovic Out 3 Months After Knee Surgery |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hawks/news/bogdan-bogdanovic-out-3-months-after-knee-surgery |access-date=12 June 2022 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}{{cite news |title=Atlanta Hawks' Bogdan Bogdanovic undergoes knee surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34092972/atlanta-hawks-bogdan-bogdanovic-undergoes-knee-surgery |access-date=15 June 2022 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |date=14 June 2022}} On 16 March 2023, he signed a four-year, $68 million contract extension with the Hawks.{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Bogdan Bogdanovic to Multi-Year Extension |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-bogdan-bogdanovic-to-multi-year-extension |access-date=16 March 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}{{Cite web |title=NBA Rumors: Bogdan Bogdanović, Hawks Agree to 4-Year, $68M Contract Extension |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10015354-nba-rumors-bogdan-bogdanovic-hawks-agree-to-4-year-68m-contract-extension |access-date=16 March 2023 |website=Bleacher Report}} On December 11, 2023, Bogdanović put up a career-high 40 points on 10 three-pointers made in a 129–122 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He also became the first player in Hawks history to put up at least 40 points and 10 three-pointers made in a game.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hawks-news-bogdan-bogdanovic-makes-bonkers-franchise-history-with-explosion-vs-nuggets|title=Hawks' Bogdan Bogdanovic makes bonkers franchise history with explosion vs. Nuggets|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=December 11, 2023|access-date=December 12, 2023}} On October 23, 2024, he was sidelined for a month with a right hamstring [[tendinopathy]] during a game against the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Bogdan Bogdanovic is out for at least one more month |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1735430/bogdan-bogdanovic-out-for-at-least-one-month-atlanta-hawks-nba/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=30 October 2024 |language=en |date=30 October 2024}} === Los Angeles Clippers (2025–2026) === On February 6, 2025, Bogdanović was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] alongside three future second-round picks in exchange for [[Terance Mann]] and [[Bones Hyland]].{{Cite web |date=2025-02-06 |title=Clippers acquire Bogan Bogdanović from Hawks in 3-player deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/clippers-hawks-trade-bogdan-bogdanovic |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} === Houston Rockets (2026–present) === On July 8, 2026, Bogdanović signed a one-year, $3.9 million contract with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Bogdan Bogdanović |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-bogdan-bogdanovic |access-date=July 8, 2026 |publisher=[[Houston Rockets]]}} ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== Bogdanović's play with [[KK Žitko Basket|Žitko]] got him a training camp invite ahead of the [[2009 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] in [[France]], however he was quickly cut by head coach [[Vlada Jovanović]] since he was about to turn 17 at that time. For his performances, he was selected to the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team]].{{cite news |title=TISSOT Most Valuable Player Rubio headlines the All-Star Five |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/tissot-most-valuable-player-rubio-headlines-the-all-star-five |access-date=15 September 2019 |work=fiba.basketball |date=15 September 2019}} With 183 points scored throughout the tournament, he was the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup Top Scorer]] by total points scored.{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/playerstats|title=total points 2019|work=fiba.com}} Bogdanović missed the [[EuroBasket 2022]] due to a right knee surgery.{{cite web |title=Srbija bez Bogdanovića na Evrobasketu! |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2022&mm=06&dd=10&nav_id=2169298 |website=b92.net |access-date=16 July 2022}} Bogdanović won silver medal at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] with the Serbia national team. He averaged 19.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.3 assists, and 2.1 steals per game. In recognition of his individual play, Bogdanović was named second time in a row to the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|World Cup All-Tournament Team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/news/dennis-schroder-named-fiba-basketball-world-cup-2023-tissot-mvp|title=Dennis Schroder named FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 Tissot MVP|publisher=[[FIBA]]|date=September 10, 2023|access-date=September 10, 2023}} He played with Serbia at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]] in Paris, and led the team with 30 points in the third group stage game against [[South Sudan men's national basketball team|South Sudan]], surpassing [[Miloš Teodosić]] to become Serbia's all-time leading scorer in all competitions by scoring his 1,058th career point.{{Cite web |date=2024-08-03 |title=Bogdanovic, Jokic hold off South Sudan, pull Greece to QFs |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/bogdanovic-jokic-hold-off-south-sudan-pull-greece-to-qfs |access-date=2024-08-04 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}} His 30-point performance also set an Olympic record for a Serbian player. He won the bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]] with Serbia.{{cite news |title=Србија освојила бронзану медаљу на Олимпијским играма! |url=https://kss.rs/srbija-osvojila-bronzanu-medalju-na-olimpijskim-igrama/ |access-date=10 August 2024 |work=kss.rs |date=10 August 2024 |language=Serbian}} Over 6 tournament games, Bogdanović averaged 18.3 points, 3.8 assists and 4 rebounds, while shooting 47.6 percent from the field, 46.2 percent from three-point range, and 92.3 percent from the free throw line. For his performances, Bogdanović was named to the tournament's All-Second Team.{{Cite web |date=2024-08-10 |title=Gilgeous-Alexander, Bogdanovic, F. Wagner, Yabusele, Antetokounmpo named to Paris 2024 All-Second Team |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/gilgeous-alexander-bogdanovic-f-wagner-yabusele-antetokounmpo-named-to-paris |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} Bogdanović was once again selected for the [[EuroBasket 2025]].
